name: Brevitus Technology
tagline: Building a modern web platform for courses, internships, and technical events
about: Brevitus Technology is a digital platform aggregating educational courses, student internships, and technical events. During a 3-month internship, I contributed to developing responsive frontend interfaces, reusable React components, and interactive user experiences across the platform.

architecture.summary: The Brevitus platform organizes courses, internships, and developer events into a cohesive web application using Next.js App Router, modular React components, and a unified design system.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.body:
Brevitus Technology is a modern web platform developed to provide access to educational courses, student internship opportunities, and developer-focused technical events through a unified digital interface.

During my 3-month internship as a Web Development Intern, I contributed directly to the platform's frontend codebase, translating design specifications into modular, accessible, and responsive Next.js components.

sections.heading: The Problem
sections.body:
Students and aspiring developers often need to explore multiple categories of opportunities—ranging from skill-building technical courses to competitive internships and local hackathons. When these opportunities are scattered across disparate channels or presented through inconsistent layouts, user discovery suffers.

The challenge was building a coherent frontend experience that unifies diverse resource types under a single, highly structured information architecture without overwhelming the user or compromising page performance.

sections.heading: The Solution & Architectural Approach
sections.body:
The engineering team adopted a component-driven frontend architecture built on Next.js and TypeScript. By establishing a shared design system with Tailwind CSS and creating specialized layouts for courses, internships, and events, the platform maintains visual and behavioral consistency across all sections.

Reusable card primitives, filtering controls, and interactive modal dialogs were engineered to support distinct metadata requirements while sharing underlying UI tokens and layout grids.

sections.heading: System Architecture & Data Flows
sections.body: The application is structured into two complementary workflows: a server-rendered page delivery path that handles routing and initial rendering, and a client-side interaction path that powers reactive filtering, search, and animation.

sections.heading: Frontend Architecture & Next.js Implementation
sections.body:
The platform leverages Next.js App Router to achieve fast page loads through server-side rendering (SSR) and file-based routing. TypeScript interfaces enforce strict contract adherence across data props, API responses, and component parameters, preventing runtime prop mismatches across pages.

State is managed locally within feature modules to avoid unnecessary re-renders, while common utilities and shared UI primitives reside in centralized component directories.

sections.heading: Responsive Design & Mobile Optimization
sections.body:
Given that a large percentage of students access educational and career portals from mobile devices, layouts were developed mobile-first:

- Flexible grid systems reflow from single-column vertical card stacks on mobile to two- and three-column grids on tablet and desktop viewports.
- Touch targets for all interactive links, badges, and filter buttons maintain a minimum 44×44px hit area to ensure comfortable mobile navigation.
- Typography uses responsive scaling and fluid clamps to prevent line-wrapping awkwardness on compact viewports.

sections.heading: Key Engineering Contributions
sections.body:
Developed responsive web interfaces across primary opportunity listing and landing pages
Engineered type-safe Next.js components utilizing TypeScript and strict prop validation
Built reusable UI card and section components used across multiple platform sections
Implemented mobile-first responsive layouts ensuring fluid viewport adaptations
Integrated smooth micro-interactions and transitions using Framer Motion
Structured course, internship, and event content presentations to optimize visual hierarchy
Ensured design consistency across platform navigation, headers, and call-to-action blocks

sections.heading: Technical Challenges & Team Collaboration
sections.body:
Contributing to an existing production codebase required rapidly assimilating established coding standards, naming conventions, and Git workflows. Balancing visual richness with rendering performance required careful restraint when applying Framer Motion animations, ensuring transitions remained performant even on low-powered mobile devices.

Collaborating with team members underscored the importance of clean documentation, modular code separation, and writing self-describing components that can be maintained effortlessly by other engineers.

sections.heading: Outcome & Professional Learnings
sections.body: The 3-month internship provided hands-on experience developing a production-oriented web platform using modern industry standards. Working with Next.js, TypeScript, and Tailwind CSS in a real-world team environment strengthened my architectural understanding of component modularity, responsive web design, and delivering seamless user experiences.
